title: Self-control
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child says self-control is choosing what is right over what a feeling pushes (Galatians 5:23-25), that it is a fruit of the Spirit, and how to avoid what defiles the body (drugs, harmful videos), even in secret.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the fruit of the Spirit.
floor.question: Which fruit of the Spirit is last in the list?

representations: a traffic light: stop, think, choose
steps: Think: does it please God and keep my body clean?
Ask the Holy Spirit for help.
contexts: a harmful video on a phone
wanting to shout at a sibling

board.do: Draw a traffic light: red stop, amber think, green choose.

board.say: What do you think about before you choose?

board.do: Wait for the child to say does it please God.
Write Galatians 5:25: keep in step with the Spirit.

misconceptions.repair: Role-play counting to ten when angry.

misconceptions.ask: Where does self-control come from, according to Galatians 5:22-25?

listen_for: Watch it, since no one will know
misconceptions.ask: A friend offers you a harmful video to watch in secret. What shows self-control?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what harm comes even if nobody finds out.

misconceptions.ask: A friend says "just try one cigarette, once is nothing". What does self-control say?
misconceptions.repair: Explain that habits start with once, and practise saying no politely but firmly.

checks.question: What is self-control?
checks.answer: Choosing what is right instead of what a feeling pushes

checks.question: Where does self-control come from, in Galatians 5?
checks.answer: It is a fruit of the Holy Spirit
